headline: Nasdaq-100 roughly unchanged after a hot August payroll print; two-sided price discovery keeps Tail low into the long weekend
body: August payrolls printed +162k against roughly 53k expected with unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% m/m, and June-July revisions added a combined 55k. The initial reaction was a good-news-is-bad-news selloff that lifted September Fed hike pricing to about 60%, yet the transmission has stayed orderly: the 10-year sits at 4.77% and the 2-year at 4.38%, both little changed on the day. The Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,450.37 low around midday and has since recovered to 29,492.13, essentially unchanged against a 29,482.32 prior close. That is a two-sided path in which retracements are occurring, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure this Tail score measures. Cross-assets conflict rather than align: VIX is at 14.08 and falling, semiconductors are firm while megacaps and a sharply lower Lululemon drag the tape. The genuine background risk is geopolitical - renewed US-Iran exchanges and reduced Strait of Hormuz transits have carried WTI to about $91 for a weekly gain near 8% - but crude is lower on the day and equities have absorbed it. That combination is scored as elevated Stress with low Tail. From 21:00 UTC futures settle for the week and the forecast reflects a halted market through the remainder of the horizon, with residual Stress representing weekend gap exposure that cannot price until Sunday.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours cover a calm overnight regime followed by the August payroll release. Tail drifted between 12% and 17% through the Asian and European sessions with Stress climbing steadily into the print. The 12:30 UTC release produced the only genuine spike, with Tail reaching 24%, Stress 76% and Confidence dropping to 74% as the event/whipsaw mode took over. Price discovery then proved orderly: Tail decayed to 20%, 18%, 17% and 15% over the following four hourly assessments as retracements appeared and volatility decayed, and the mode reverted to mixed. No hour required a blocking action.
outlookSummary: The remaining cash hours are expected to keep two-sided structure with Tail in the 13-16% band, the upper end reserved for the 19:00-21:00 UTC close window where pre-holiday position squaring can thin liquidity. US cash closes at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures settle at 21:00 UTC, after which the entire remainder of this horizon is a halted market with no live price path; forecast Tail therefore falls to 4-5% and the published dominant mode of normal denotes a closed venue rather than a resolved regime. Residual Stress in the 31-42% band carries what cannot price until the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, principally unresolved US-Iran hostilities and reduced Strait of Hormuz transits, and secondarily roughly 60% September Fed hike pricing. Monday 7 September is the Labor Day holiday, so the next US cash open is Tuesday 8 September, and the next scheduled US data of consequence is PPI and jobless claims on Thursday 10 September followed by August CPI on Friday 11 September.
